scope: Nine sentence-audited residual tokens in the base papers: one malformed ASCII takozhe and all eight non-headword tuta/Tuta occurrences.
choice: Normalize takozhe to official takože. Split tuta/Tuta by grammatical function: four adverbial German hier contexts become tu/Tu, while four attributive German dieser/dieses/diese contexts become agreeing ta/Ta.
motivation: The eight tuta surfaces conflate two distinct official paradigms. Official tu is the type-1 adverb here; official toj (feminine ta, neuter to) is the primary demonstrative this/that. Exact German alignment and noun agreement make the partition deterministic. The ASCII digraph takozhe is not an ISV form and is a one-site transliteration residue beside 1005 established takože controls.
alternatives_rejected: Blind tuta to tu was rejected because four sites modify explicit feminine nouns and translate German demonstratives rather than the adverb here.
Blind tuta to ta was rejected because four sites translate German hier and are syntactically adverbial.
Retaining official type-2 tut was rejected because the current surface tuta is not that headword and because the edition already establishes the broader type-1 tu family.
Retaining takozhe as an ASCII transliteration was rejected because official orthography and the established edition form are takože.

validation.coverage: All nine exact locators are required once and the applicator refuses any source-count or locator drift.
validation.postcondition: Whole-token takozhe, Tuta and tuta all become zero; the five established target forms rise by exactly the mapped counts.
validation.structure: Line count, raw brace counts, ordered TeX-control stream and math-delimiter stream are invariant; Work 44, Paper 45 and bibliography are byte-identical.
validation.reproducibility: The deterministic applicator binds all four input and output byte counts and SHA-256 hashes.
